info.title: Sinatra API
info.description: Start, follow and stop Sinatra tasks, and delegate Linear and GitHub issues. Send your token on every request as `Authorization: Bearer sntr_...`, or the access token the CLI's browser sign-in gets. Bodies are JSON. A workspace you don't belong to answers `404`, never `403`.

get.description: Returns the user the token acts as and the workspaces they belong to, ordered by name. Use it to find the workspace ids the other endpoints take.

401.description:
Unauthorized. The `error` code says which:

- `invalid_token`: The token is missing, malformed, expired or revoked, or it's an OAuth access token issued for Sinatra's MCP server rather than this API.

429.description:
Too many requests. The `error` code says which:

- `bad_request`: You're over the request rate limit: 600 GET requests a minute, or 120 POST or DELETE requests a minute, per token and per endpoint. Wait the seconds in the `Retry-After` header, then retry.

500.description:
Internal server error. The `error` code says which:

- `internal_error`: Something went wrong on Sinatra's side. Retry; if it keeps happening, share the `x-request-id` header with support.

delete.description: Revokes the token that sends the request, and answers `204` with no body. Requests with that token get `401 invalid_token` afterwards. A token from a browser sign-in is revoked together with the rest of that sign-in. `sinatra logout` calls this when you logged in with a token.

204.description: The token is revoked. There is no body.

get.description:
Lists the workspace's tasks, from every source, most recently active first.

To get the next page, pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. Treat the cursor as opaque. `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only tasks in this status, such as `implementing` or `pr_open`. A name that isn't a task status is `invalid_status`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many tasks to return, 1 to 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page. Treat it as opaque.

200.description: A page of tasks, most recently active first.

400.description:
Bad request. The `error` code says which:

- `invalid_cursor`: `cursor` isn't a well-formed cursor. Pass back a `nextCursor` unchanged.
- `invalid_limit`: `limit` isn't a whole number from 1 to 100.
- `invalid_status`: No task status has that name.

post.description:
Starts a task and returns `202` with the task and the id of your first message. The task runs like any other: it gets a sandbox, can open a pull request, and shows up in the dashboard.

Only `prompt` is required. `title` defaults to the prompt's first line, up to 80 characters. `repo` is optional: omit it to let the agent choose a repository.

Before it makes the task, Sinatra checks that the workspace is connected to GitHub when the start names a repository (without GitHub a task that names none can still answer, research or plan), that billing allows the task, and that the queue has room. A refusal says which in its `error` code, and a retry with the same key of a start that already made its task is never refused.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry is safe. A start retried with the same key returns the same task and never starts a second one. The same key with a different prompt, or a different repository or title if you send them, is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Keys belong to the person who sent them. The key becomes the first message's `messageId`.

If Sinatra saves your request but can't hand it to the agent yet, it answers `503 unavailable` with the new `taskId` and `messageId`. Retry with the same key, or send a message on that task, which sends your prompt first.

A task started this way counts against the workspace's plan like any other. A running turn takes one of the plan's tasks at a time; past that it's queued. See [How the queue works](https://docs.sinatra.dev/docs/managed/billing#how-the-queue-works). It also needs model access, like a task delegated from Linear or GitHub. See [Models](https://docs.sinatra.dev/docs/configuration/models).

202.description: The task started. The agent is picking it up.

400.description:
Bad request. The `error` code says which:

- `bad_request`: The body isn't valid JSON, or is empty.
- `invalid_idempotency_key`: The `Idempotency-Key` isn't 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters, with no spaces.
- `invalid_prompt`: `prompt` is missing, empty, or over 100,000 characters. A body not sent as `application/json` has no `prompt`.
- `invalid_repo`: `repo` isn't a repository connected to the workspace.
- `invalid_title`: `title` is empty or over 200 characters.

401.description:
Unauthorized. The `error` code says which:

- `invalid_token`: The token is missing, malformed, expired or revoked, or it's an OAuth access token issued for Sinatra's MCP server rather than this API.

404.description:
Not found. The `error` code says which:

- `not_found`: The workspace doesn't exist, or you aren't a member of it. The API answers 404 and never 403, so it doesn't reveal which workspaces exist.

409.description:
Conflict. The `error` code says which:

- `capacity_full`: The workspace's queue is full. `reason` is the message to show, the same one the dashboard shows. When starting a task, the body also has `plan`, `running`, `queued` and `billingUrl`.
- `github_not_connected`: The start names a repository but the workspace isn't connected to GitHub (`refusal` is `missing`), or its GitHub App installation is suspended (`refusal` is `suspended`). Without GitHub, a start that names no repository runs: it can answer, research or plan. `reason` says what to do and ends with `settingsUrl`: the workspace's Integrations settings, where an owner or admin connects GitHub, or the installation's page on GitHub when it's suspended.
- `idempotency_conflict`: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a start with a different prompt, or a different repository or title if the retry sends them.
- `payment_required`: Billing would stop the task: you have no model access in this workspace (`refusal` is `own_credentials_required`), or its subscription is past due (`refusal` is `subscription_inactive`). `reason` says what to do and ends with `billingUrl`, the settings section that fixes it: your model credentials for `own_credentials_required`, billing for `subscription_inactive`.

post.description:
Sends a follow-up on a task and returns `202` with the message's id.

Any member of the workspace can follow up on a task started from the API, CLI, MCP or dashboard. Follow up on other tasks, such as Linear or GitHub issues, where they started; here they return `409 not_an_api_task`. A task that has been idle for a while picks up again when you follow up.

A message sent while the agent is working doesn't change the current turn. It waits and runs as the next turn. A message isn't refused when the workspace is running its limit of tasks: its turn takes a place in the queue, and if the queue is full, the refusal appears in the task's conversation instead.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry is safe: a message retried with the same key is sent once. Keys belong to their sender, so two people using the same key send two messages. The key becomes the message's `messageId`.

If Sinatra saves the message but can't hand it to the agent yet, it answers `503 unavailable` with the `messageId`. Retry with that `messageId` as the `Idempotency-Key`, so the message is sent once.

202.description: The message was sent. The agent runs it as the task's next turn.

Bad request. The `error` code says which:

- `bad_request`: The body isn't valid JSON, or is empty.
- `invalid_idempotency_key`: The `Idempotency-Key` isn't 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters, with no spaces.
- `invalid_prompt`: `text` is missing, empty, or over 100,000 characters. A body not sent as `application/json` has no `text`.

- `not_an_api_task`: The task started elsewhere, such as in Linear or GitHub, so it has no conversation here. Follow up where it started.

get.description:
Returns the conversation of a task started from the API, CLI, MCP or dashboard, oldest first. A task that started elsewhere has no conversation here (`409 not_an_api_task`); its conversation is where it started.

The conversation holds final answers and questions, not progress. The agent posts one reply per turn: its answer, or a question when it needs your input. Sinatra adds its own notices, such as errors and refusals.

Each entry's `role` and `kind` say what it is:

- `user` and `message`: a message a person sent. `messageId` is its idempotency key, or a generated id.
- `agent` and `response`: the agent's answer for a turn.
- `agent` and `clarify`: a question the agent needs answered to continue.
- `platform` and `response` or `error`: a message from Sinatra itself, such as a refusal, an error, a stop, or files the agent produced.

When `next` isn't `null`, more entries follow: pass `next` as `after` to get the next page.

There is no streaming. To wait for a reply, poll this endpoint with `after` set to the `id` of the last entry you read, and check the task's `status` with Get a task. The turn is done when the task stops working, for example when it reaches `replied` or `pr_open`. While a task is queued, its conversation stays quiet; its `queued` field says so.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `id` of the last entry you've read. Returns only later entries. An id that isn't an entry of this task is `invalid_cursor`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many entries to return, 1 to 200.

200.description: A page of the conversation, oldest first.

400.description:
Bad request. The `error` code says which:

- `invalid_cursor`: `after` isn't an entry of this task's conversation, for example an id from another task.
- `invalid_limit`: `limit` isn't a whole number from 1 to 200.

get.description:
Lists the open Linear and GitHub issues you could delegate. It is the same list as the dashboard's ticket picker: yours first, then your team's unassigned ones, Linear's before GitHub's, at most 10 from each tracker.

Issues assigned to someone else, closed, or already being worked on are left out, and so are pull requests. Linear issues appear only when your Linear account is linked, and are read as you. GitHub issues appear only if you have a GitHub account, and only from the repositories enabled in the workspace.

To delegate one, pass a Linear issue's `identifier` as `id`, or a GitHub issue's `identifier` split into `repo` and `number`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text to match: GitHub search terms, and a substring of a Linear issue's title. Up to 200 characters.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: `owner/name` of an enabled repository to search first on GitHub. A repository that isn't enabled is ignored.

200.description: The issues you could delegate, and the workspace's tracker connections.

post.description:
Hands Sinatra an existing Linear or GitHub issue as you, as if you'd assigned it to Sinatra yourself, and returns `202` with `{"ok": true}`. The task then runs on the issue. Its conversation is there, not under Read the conversation, and it appears in List tasks once Sinatra picks it up.

The rules match delegating from the dashboard. Sinatra reads a Linear issue as your linked Linear account, so you can only delegate issues you can see. Closed issues, pull requests and issues assigned to someone else are refused. If the workspace's queue is full, the request is refused before the issue is touched.

A refusal returns an `error` code and a `reason` that says what to fix, for example `{"error": "linear_identity_unlinked", "reason": "Connect your Linear account in Settings to search and delegate Linear issues."}`.

202.description: The issue was delegated. Sinatra picks it up on its tracker.

400.description:
Bad request. The `error` code says which:

- `assigned_to_other`: The issue is assigned to someone else.
- `bad_request`: The body isn't valid JSON, or is empty.
- `github_identity_required`: Your Sinatra user has no connected GitHub account, which delegating a GitHub issue needs.
- `invalid_body`: The body doesn't name an issue. Send `source` with `id` for Linear, or with `repo` and `number` for GitHub, as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`.
- `invalid_repo`: `repo` isn't in `owner/name` form.
- `issue_closed`: The issue is already closed.
- `linear_app_user_missing`: The workspace's Linear connection has to be redone so Sinatra can be assigned issues. Reconnect Linear in the workspace's settings.
- `linear_identity_conflict`: Your Linear account is linked to another Sinatra account in this workspace, so connecting it again won't help. Ask a workspace owner to remove that binding in Settings.
- `linear_identity_unlinked`: Your Linear account isn't connected in this workspace, so Sinatra can't read Linear as you. Connect your Linear account in Settings first.
- `linear_not_connected`: The workspace isn't connected to Linear.
- `not_an_issue`: The number is a pull request. Only issues can be delegated.
- `repo_disabled`: The repository isn't enabled in the workspace. Enable it in Settings first.

401.description:
Unauthorized. The `error` code says which:

- `invalid_token`: The token is missing, malformed, expired or revoked, or it's an OAuth access token issued for Sinatra's MCP server rather than this API.

404.description:
Not found. The `error` code says which:

- `issue_not_found`: There is no issue with that id that Sinatra can see. A Linear issue is read as your linked Linear account, so you can only delegate issues you can see.
- `not_found`: The workspace doesn't exist, or you aren't a member of it. The API answers 404 and never 403, so it doesn't reveal which workspaces exist.

409.description:
Conflict. The `error` code says which:

- `capacity_full`: The workspace's queue is full, so the issue is refused before it is touched. `reason` is the message to show, the same one the dashboard shows.
- `linear_reconnect_required`: Linear stopped accepting the workspace's Linear connection. A workspace owner or admin has to reconnect Linear in the workspace's settings.

text.description: The message, up to 100,000 characters after trimming.

CreateMessageRequest.description: A message to send on a task.

messageId.description: The message's id: the `Idempotency-Key` you sent, or a generated id.

prompt.description: What to do, as you'd ask a teammate. Up to 100,000 characters, after trimming.

title.description: The task's title, up to 200 characters. Defaults to the prompt's first line, cut to 80 characters.

repo.description: `owner/name` of a repository connected to the workspace. Omit it to let the agent choose.

messageId.description: The id of your first message: the `Idempotency-Key` you sent, or a generated id.

CreateTaskResponse.description: The task that started, and the id of your first message.

repo.description: `owner/name` of a repository enabled in the workspace.

number.description: The issue's number in that repository.

DelegateGithubTicket.description: A GitHub issue to delegate, by its repository and number.

id.description: The issue's identifier, such as `ENG-123`, or its id.

DelegateLinearTicket.description: A Linear issue to delegate, by its identifier or id.

DelegateTicketRequest.description: An issue to delegate: a Linear issue by `id`, or a GitHub issue by `repo` and `number`.

ok.description: Always `true`: the issue was handed to Sinatra.

error.description: A machine-readable code, such as `invalid_prompt`. Branch on this, not on `reason`. New codes can appear. Known codes: `assigned_to_other`, `bad_request`, `capacity_full`, `github_identity_required`, `github_not_connected`, `github_rate_limited`, `idempotency_conflict`, `internal_error`, `invalid_body`, `invalid_cursor`, `invalid_idempotency_key`, `invalid_limit`, `invalid_prompt`, `invalid_repo`, `invalid_status`, `invalid_title`, `invalid_token`, `issue_closed`, `issue_not_found`, `linear_app_user_missing`, `linear_identity_conflict`, `linear_identity_unlinked`, `linear_not_connected`, `linear_reconnect_required`, `not_an_api_task`, `not_an_issue`, `not_found`, `not_running`, `payment_required`, `repo_disabled`, `unavailable`.

reason.description: A sentence saying what went wrong and, where it helps, what to do. Written to show to a person.

requestId.description: The request's id. Present on some errors, not all; the `x-request-id` response header always carries it. Share it with support.

refusal.description: Why a start was refused, on `payment_required` and `github_not_connected`. For `payment_required`: `own_credentials_required` or `subscription_inactive`. For `github_not_connected`: `missing` or `suspended`.

billingUrl.description: The settings section that fixes the refusal: your model credentials or billing, on `payment_required`; billing, when starting a task, on `capacity_full`.

settingsUrl.description: The settings page that fixes the refusal, on `github_not_connected`.

plan.description: The workspace's plan, on `capacity_full` when starting a task.

running.description: How many tasks the plan runs at a time, on `capacity_full` when starting a task.

queued.description: How many tasks the plan queues, on `capacity_full` when starting a task.

taskId.description: On `unavailable` after a start: the task that was made. Retry with the same key, or send a message on it.

messageId.description: On `unavailable`: the message that was saved but not sent yet. Retry with it as the `Idempotency-Key`.

Error.description: The body of every error response.

githubLogin.description: The user's GitHub login. `null` for a user without GitHub.

name.description: The user's name, if they have one.

email.description: The user's email address: the one they sign in with by email, or their primary GitHub email.

user.description: The user the token acts as.

workspaces.description: The workspaces the user belongs to, ordered by name.

id.description: The entry's id. Pass the last one you read as `after` to get only later entries.

messageId.description: For a message a person sent: the id it was sent with, which is its idempotency key or a generated id. `null` on every other entry.

role.description: Who wrote it: `user` for a person, `agent` for the agent, `platform` for Sinatra itself. New roles can appear.

kind.description: What it is: `message` (a person's message), `response` (the agent's answer for a turn, or a notice from Sinatra such as a stop or files the agent produced), `clarify` (a question the agent needs answered to continue) or `error` (a refusal or failure from Sinatra). New kinds can appear.

Message.description: An entry in a task's conversation.

next.description: When it isn't `null`, more entries follow: pass it as `after` to get them. `null` on the last page.

MessageList.description: A page of a task's conversation.

url.description: The pull request's address on GitHub.

merged.description: `true` once the pull request is merged.

PullRequest.description: The pull request a task opened.

accepted.description: Always `true`: the task was told to stop.

id.description: The task's id. Use it as `taskId` in the task endpoints.

status.description: Where the task is in its life, such as `pending`, `implementing`, `replied`, `pr_open` or `completed`. New statuses can appear, so don't treat the list as closed. See [Raw statuses](https://docs.sinatra.dev/docs/getting-started/how-it-works#raw-statuses) for each one.

source.description: Where the task started: `api` for the CLI, MCP, this API or the dashboard, `linear` or `github_issue` for an issue, `slack` or `telegram` for a chat. Other sources can appear, so treat an unknown value as a task started elsewhere.

title.description: The task's title. `null` for a task whose issue has no title.

repo.description: `owner/name` of the task's repository. `null` until a repository is chosen.

pullRequest.description: The task's pull request. `null` until one opens.

queued.description: `true` while a turn waits because the workspace is already running as many tasks at a time as its plan allows. The dashboard shows this as Queued.

lastActivityAt.description: When the task last did something. `null` if it hasn't yet.

url.description: The task's page in the Sinatra dashboard, where anyone in the workspace can follow it. On a task started from the CLI, MCP, API or dashboard they can reply there too.

Task.description: A task: one piece of work Sinatra does, from any source.

tasks.description: The page's tasks, most recently active first.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` to get the next page. Treat it as opaque. `null` on the last page.

id.description: The issue's id on Sinatra's side. For GitHub it looks like `github:owner/name#42`.

source.description: Where the issue lives: `linear` or `github`. New sources can appear.

identifier.description: What to delegate it by. A Linear identifier such as `ENG-123` (send it as `id`), or a GitHub `owner/name#42` (send `owner/name` as `repo` and `42` as `number`).

yours.description: `true` if the issue is assigned to you or you wrote it.

state.description: A GitHub issue's state, such as `open`. `null` for a Linear issue.

context.description: The Linear team's name, or the GitHub repository's name.

url.description: The issue's address on its tracker.

workspaceId.description: The id of the workspace that was searched.

workspaceLabel.description: The name the dashboard's ticket picker gives that workspace.

Ticket.description: An open issue you could delegate to Sinatra.

tickets.description: The issues you could delegate. Linear issues come first, then GitHub's, each with yours before your team's unassigned ones.

connected.description: Whether the workspace is connected to Linear.

identityLinked.description: Whether your Linear account is linked in this workspace. Linear issues are listed only when it is.

identityBound.description: Whether your Linear identity is tied to your Sinatra user.

linear.description: The workspace's Linear connection, as it applies to you.

connected.description: Whether the workspace is connected to GitHub.

repo.description: The repository the GitHub search covered, when the `repo` query matched an enabled one and had open issues. Otherwise `null`.

TicketSearchResult.description: The issues you could delegate, and how the workspace is connected to each tracker.

id.description: The workspace's id. Use it as `workspaceId` in the workspace endpoints.

role.description: Your role in it: `owner`, `admin` or `member`. New roles can appear.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe. 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters, with no spaces. A request repeated with the same key answers with the first one's result and does the work once; the same key with different content is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Keys belong to the person who sent them: two people using the same key start two tasks or send two messages. The key is also the `messageId` of the message the request sends, which is a start's first message.

RequestId.description: The request's id, to share with support.

bearerAuth.description: A personal access token, which starts with `sntr_`. Create one on the dashboard's CLI & API page (https://app.sinatra.dev/tokens). It acts as you in every workspace you belong to, with your role in each, and expires after at most 365 days. The CLI's browser sign-in sends an OAuth access token here instead.
